body:
Problem:
  If you want a custom `reuse_client` in a public lsp config, you first have
  to copy the whole default matching logic, because `reuse_client_default` is
  local. That's ~30 lines just to add one extra check.

  Solution:
  Expose it as `vim.lsp.reuse_client_default` so configs can build on top of
  the default instead of reimplementing it:

      reuse_client = function(client, config)
        return vim.lsp.reuse_client_default(client, config) and my_check(config)
      end

  This covers the "default plus an extra condition" case. The gopls example in
  the issue is "default OR a per-folder override", which would also want
  `_get_workspace_folders` exposed, but I left that out for now.

  Closes #41552

comment_regular_data.body:
> This feels like a "reverse" extensibility hook. This function is small enough that I don't see the issue in copy-pasting it.

the reason i went with exposing it is that copies go stale. in nvim-lspconfig the configs are public and touched
  by lots of people, so if someone copies reuse_client_default and the real one changes later, their copy is
  silently wrong. that already happened when bufnr got added to the predicate. calling the default directly just
  stays correct.

  but if you'd rather keep it private and just document it somewhere, then there's probably no need for this PR and i'm
  happy to close it.

Hello @alarcritty
Thank you for your time and efforts with this pr.

I am agree with @MariaSolOs in part that `reuse_client_default` function should not be exposed.
IMHO, what should be exposed are client and workspace detection default logic separately.

Unfortunately this example is logically wrong, because if `reuse_client_default` fails on client or workspace detection, we never get custom condition. 
```lua
reuse_client = function(client, config)
  return vim.lsp.reuse_client_default(client, config) and my_check(config)
end
```
I think, it would be reasonable to split `reuse_client_default` logic in separate functions for client and workspace detection, end expose those functions.

<details>
<summary>
example (edited: fixed conditions in `reuse_client_default`)
</summary>

```lua
local function _reusable_client_default(client, config)
  return client.name == config.name and not client:is_topped()
end

function lsp.reusable_client_default(client, config)
  return _reusable_client_default(client, config)
end

local function _reusable_workspace_default(client, config)
  local config_folders = lsp._get_workspace_folders(config.workspace_folders or config.root_dir)

  if not config_folders or not next(config_folders) then
    -- Reuse if the client was configured with no workspace folders
    local client_config_folders =
      lsp._get_workspace_folders(client.config.workspace_folders or client.config.root_dir)
    return not client_config_folders or not next(client_config_folders)
  end

  for _, config_folder in ipairs(config_folders) do
    for _, client_folder in ipairs(client.workspace_folders or {}) do
      if config_folder.uri == client_folder.uri then
        return true
      end
    end
  end

  return false
end

function lsp.reusable_workspace_default(client, config)
  return _reusable_workspace_default(client, config)
end

local function reuse_client_default(client, config)
  if not _reusable_client_default(client, config) then
    return false
  end

  if  _reusable_workspace_default(client, config) then
    return true
  end

  return false
end
```
</details> 

Such separation would allow users to build their own reuse logic using defaults if needed. (edited: fixed conditions in `reuse_client`)
```lua
reuse_client = function(client, config, bufnr)
  if not vim.lsp.reusable_client_default(client, config) then
    return false
  end

  if vim.lsp.reusable_workspace_default(client, config) then
    return true
  end

  if custom_condition(client, config, bufnr) then
    return true
  end

  return false
end
```
